turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala turned to Sandip and asked why he was being so obstinate, and what was it about Nikhil's warning that he found so hard to accept.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Bimala that he was not being obstinate, he was just bored with Nikhil's theatrics and that the real show was about to begin, not the one Nikhil was trying to put on.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Bimala that Nikhil's warning was a thinly veiled attempt to intimidate him, and that he wouldn't be swayed by such tactics.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip sneered at Nikhil's warnings, calling them 'fear-mongering fantasies' and saying that the only thing Nikhil was truly afraid of was losing his own power and influence.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant attitude was a testament to his own lack of foresight and that the Mussulman attacks would not be a mere fantasy, but a harsh reality.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala turned to Nikhil and asked if there was any truth to the rumors of tensions between the Mussulmans and the Hindu community in the region.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the information he had received from his informants was credible and that the situation was indeed volatile, and he urged Sandip to take immediate action to protect his estate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and said that Nikhil's warnings were starting to sound like a tired refrain, a broken record of fear and uncertainty.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he would not stand idly by while his rival's carelessness put the entire region at risk, and that he would take whatever measures necessary to protect his own estate and family.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that his informants had provided concrete evidence of the Mussulmans' intentions, and that the situation was far more perilous than Sandip seemed to comprehend.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil to explain the nature of this 'concrete evidence' he mentioned, her voice calm and inquiring as she turned her gaze towards him.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil to clarify the implications of this perceived threat on the zamindari's relationships with the local Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil what specific measures he had taken to address the situation, and how he proposed to mitigate the risks to both estates.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was starting to get bored with the endless warnings and threats, and that perhaps it was time to actually do something about the situation, rather than just sitting around talking about it

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had considered the potential consequences of escalating tensions between the zamindari and the local Mussulmans, and whether he believed Sandip's dismissal of the situation was entirely unreasonable.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was so fond of being the village gossip, why he couldn't come up with anything more original than 'attacks from the Mussulmans' every five minutes.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil explained that the situation was not something to be taken lightly, and that the zamindari's security was his top priority.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was starting to think that his rival was secretly enjoying the drama and the attention that came with it

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip scoffed that Nikhil was just trying to frighten him into submission, and that his rival's warnings were nothing but a thinly veiled attempt to undermine his authority as a zamindar

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil cautioned Sandip that he would not be swayed by frivolous remarks and that the well-being of the zamindari was far more important than petty squabbles.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
